bug_semantics: WEBrick's chunked-body reader ends with `read_header(socket)  # trailer + CRLF` (lib/webrick/httprequest.rb, read_chunked), which unconditionally re-invokes the same header parser used for the initial request head: `@header = HTTPUtils::parse_header(@raw_header.join)` overwrites the canonical request-header hash with the trailer block, then `@header.delete("transfer-encoding")` erases the only record that the request was Transfer-Encoding: chunked. A client can therefore smuggle `Content-Length: N` as a chunked TRAILER: the initial head says `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` (so the CL-vs-TE conflict check in read_body never fires because read_body's self['content-length'] test runs before the trailer reparse), the trailer's Content-Length is parsed straight into @header as canonical request state, and transfer-encoding is then deleted — leaving a request whose canonical state claims both a Content-Length body framing that the server never consumed and no TE marker. Downstream, @remaining_size is reset to 0 while @header['content-length'] survives, so any component that later trusts self['content-length'] (e.g. meta["CONTENT_LENGTH"] in CGI/ERB env setup, or keep-alive pipelining logic) interprets the unread socket bytes as the next request — classic CL-via-trailer request smuggling (CWE-444). The advisory scope is 'through v1.9.2', i.e. every tagged release.

Original analysis retained for provenance: Vulnerability first: the advisory names the mechanism — WEBrick reparses trailer Content-Length into canonical request state through v1.9.2 (CWE-444 request smuggling). Code archaeology pinned the exact sink: read_chunked's trailing `read_header(socket)  # trailer + CRLF` reuses the request-head parser, overwriting @header with the trailer block and then deleting transfer-encoding, so a chunked trailer's Content-Length becomes canonical request framing state after the CL-vs-TE rejection window has passed. BIC selection: `git log -S 'trailer + CRLF'` returns exactly one commit — the 2003-07-23 git-svn import 037e8523 that created lib/webrick/httprequest.rb with the sink already present; parent 392296c has no such file (verified via git cat-file -e), so this is the smallest surviving first-write in public history and a valid BIC under the protocol (svn prehistory is a genuine public-history boundary, and the immediate parent is verifiable). The flaw is single-commit: squash_decomposed=false with empty decomposed_shas — later smuggling hardening (f5faca9, 2024) and the EOFError/CRLF commit (2b38d561, 2024) touched adjacent lines but did not introduce or extend the trailer-reparse design. Tag cross-check: BIC is an ancestor of v1.9.2 and of every tag back to v1.4.0, covering the full disclosed range. AI decision, BIC-only: the BIC commit object carries a lone human identity (gotoyuzo, 2003, git-svn import message, no trailers) and the marker grep found nothing (NONE-037E) — verdict NOT_AI; markers on the fix object (none found there either) would be evidence-only regardless. Fix: 25b0e920 (Jeremy Evans, 2026-07-18, 'Only allow specific trailers', fixes #198 via PR #199) restructures trailer handling into a separate hash with a content-length disallow-list; it is merged at HEAD but in no tag yet, so fix_sha and direct_fix_sha both point to that single mainline commit while the newest release v1.9.2 remains vulnerable, exactly matching the advisory's 'through v1.9.2' range.
